content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Summary of the review (INDEMN — deviation, preferred target):**

- **What exists:** Section 14.1 already gives us a RevMed defend/indemnify/hold-harmless obligation covering Sanofi and its Affiliates against Third Party Claims arising from RevMed's negligence, recklessness or willful misconduct and its breaches of warranties/obligations (which, with the Section 13.4(b) compliance covenant, captures breach of Applicable Law). Section 14.3 supplies notice, control of defence and cooperation.
- **The gap:** no limb reaches Third Party IP infringement/misappropriation, and Section 13.5 expressly disclaims any non-infringement warranty; Section 10.7 only requires the parties to negotiate a Third Party licence (and gives Sanofi the first burden). That is the playbook's walk-away case, so the clause fails even the fallback.
- **Why preferred, not fallback:** the fallback's 3× annual-fees super-cap would cut back an indemnity that is currently uncapped (Section 14.5 preserves indemnity claims), and "annual fees" has no analogue in this upfront/milestone/royalty structure — we do not weaken our own position to reach a checklist element.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** new limbs (d) IP infringement/misappropriation by the RevMed Licensed Technology or our exercise of the licences and (e) unauthorised access to or disclosure of Sanofi Confidential Information/data caused by RevMed, with the "(a) through (c)" cross-reference conformed to "(e)"; and Section 14.2 narrowed to Sanofi-provided content and Sanofi's breach of Applicable Law.
